record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the Gaussian structure in Grothendieck’s inequality over both R and C can be replaced by tail-dependent distribution functions, such as generalized extreme value distributions, or by infinitely divisible probability distributions, while preserving the inequality; if such replacement is possible, determine whether it can improve the lower or upper bounds for the Grothendieck constant and whether correlation matrices still suffice in the trace-inequality formulation.

evidence.quote: We finish this research list with a few completely open questions and a conclusion: Can we remove the underlying Gaussian structure in Grothendieck’s inequality (for both fields, R and C) and implement tail dependent distribution functions instead (such as the generalized extreme value (GEV) distribution) and maintain the inequality? If this were the case, could that approach also be used to improve the lower and the upper bound of the Grothendieck constant? What about infinitely divisible probability distributions in general? It is very likely that just the use of correlation matrices in the trace inequality version of GT would then no longer suffice.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Grothendieck's inequality states that there exists a finite universal constant K (depending on the scalar field F = R or C) such that for every integer n ≥ 1, every n × n matrix (a_{ij}) with scalar entries, and every choice of unit vectors x_1,…,x_n, y_1,…,y_n in a Hilbert space H over F,

   |Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} ⟨x_i, y_j⟩| ≤ K · sup{ |Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} s_i t_j| : |s_i|, |t_j| ≤ 1, s_i, t_j ∈ F }.

The smallest such K is the Grothendieck constant K_G^F. A standard route to the inequality realizes the inner product ⟨x_i, y_j⟩ via expectations of the form E[f(⟨x_i, g⟩) f(⟨y_j, g⟩)] for a standard Gaussian vector g and a suitable function f, and an equivalent "trace-inequality" formulation expresses the bound in terms of correlation matrices arising from such Gaussian expectations.

Problem. Investigate whether the underlying Gaussian probabilistic structure used in proofs of Grothendieck's inequality, over both F = R and F = C, can be replaced by another class of probability distributions while still yielding an inequality of the same form with a finite constant. Specifically:

(a) Can the Gaussian distribution be replaced by a tail-dependent distribution function — for example, a generalized extreme value (GEV) distribution (Gumbel, Fréchet, or Weibull type) — in such a way that the resulting inequality continues to hold with a finite universal constant?

(b) Can it be replaced more generally by an infinitely divisible probability distribution on R^d (or C^d), so that an analogue of Grothendieck's inequality is obtained?

(c) If such replacements are possible, can the resulting framework yield improved upper bounds, or improved lower bounds, on the Grothendieck constants K_G^R and K_G^C compared with the bounds known from the Gaussian approach?

(d) In any such non-Gaussian replacement, determine whether the trace-inequality reformulation of Grothendieck's inequality can still be expressed purely in terms of correlation matrices, or whether one must instead use a strictly larger class of dependence objects (e.g., copulas or general joint distribution functions encoding tail dependence).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work establishing a Grothendieck-type inequality with the Gaussian structure replaced by GEV or general infinitely divisible distributions, nor any improvement of the Grothendieck constants by such methods. The question is posed explicitly as an open research direction, and no resolution appears to be available in the literature.

status_evidence.claim: Standard references on Grothendieck's inequality rely on the Gaussian/Hilbert-space framework and do not record a non-Gaussian replacement.
